title: an assertion that relabels a Clock layer as a Directory layer does not make it provide Directory; the provide is refused for Directory by name
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Layer Algebra': 'A layer MUST associate each capability's nominal context key with a compatible service instance.' The association is made by the `Layer.succeed(Clock, clock)` CALL — it is what the runtime registry keys on — and `as unknown as Layer<typeof Directory>` is erased before anything runs. So the layer provides Clock, the body requires Directory, and the only closed answer is refusal naming Directory. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: its sibling `a-layer-through-a-type-only-wrapper-is-the-same-layer` requires the compiler to see THROUGH `satisfies`, `as`, `<T>` and `as unknown as`, and there are two ways to satisfy that requirement. One strips the wrapper and reads the operand's syntax. The other asks the checker for the wrapped expression's TYPE, which is `Layer<typeof Directory>` here, and reads the capability out of that — and it passes every one of the eight accepting spellings, because in all eight the asserted type is true. This program is the one where it is false, and it is the reason the accepting case cannot be trusted alone: a type-reading resolver certifies this program as fully provided, and the program then panics at run time with an unsatisfied Directory requirement, because the registry holds Clock. That is a fail-open certified by a green corpus. A measured instance of exactly this hazard exists one argument away and is NOT this case — laundering at the CAPABILITY argument (`Layer.succeed(Directory as unknown as typeof Clock, clock)`) is a live divergence today: the fork reads the checker type there, accepts, and panics. It is deliberately left out, because a case for it would have to be marked `xfail` on the fork, and this case is written so that closing that one does not require touching this file. WHAT THIS CASE PINS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: it pins the code, the authored position, and that the refusal names Directory. `messageContains` is declared because the payload IS the promise: code and position alone are satisfied by a refusal naming Clock, and 'Clock is missing' is exactly what a resolver that believed the assertion and then confused the two sets would say. The bare capability name is the smallest fragment carrying it on both backends, which render the row differently (`Directory` versus `{Directory}`). It does not pin `SMITHERS2104`: the layer is NOT opaque, it is perfectly readable and provides the wrong thing, and answering 'opaque' here would be a different and worse diagnosis. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column from 26 to 23 — the column its `satisfies`-wrapped sibling reports, so the mutation is a plausible one rather than a nonsense one — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 889e30e7a81091a6ec760428c676115fe1bb4a3812db0a6af8baa6d9114d11e6 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive control is `a-layer-through-a-type-only-wrapper-is-the-same-layer`, whose fourth line is `as unknown as Layer<typeof Directory>` over a Directory layer and must keep compiling AND RUNNING: a resolver that refuses every double assertion turns that case red rather than passing this one for the wrong reason.
